title: Allocation Schemes in Analytic Evaluation: Applicant-Centric Holistic or Attribute-Centric Segmented?
benchmark_measurement: Not applicable. The paper does not conduct a benchmark or measure any aspect related to faith or religion. Its focus is on comparing 'holistic' versus 'segmented' evaluation schemes by human evaluators in terms of calibration, efficiency, and general bias.
findings: The paper does not contain any findings related to religion, as it was not a subject of the study. The key findings relate to the tradeoffs between holistic and segmented evaluation schemes: segmented allocation improves evaluator calibration accuracy, while holistic allocation can be more efficient, especially when applicant attributes are highly correlated. The paper also finds that the impact on mitigating bias depends on specific parameters of the situation.
